newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss komax in mbo, plans ipo in two years.
newsitem.headline: Swiss komax in mbo, plans ipo in two years.

text.p: Max Koch, sole owner of komax AG, a leading producer of wire processing systems, has sold the company to its management and SBC Equity Partners AG, a unit of Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) that specialises in management buyouts.
In order to raise funds for the long-term growth of komax and expansion into Asia and Latin America, komax plans a stock market listing in around two years, a statement from komax said.
Komax' management is headed by Leo Steiner, who has been in charge of operations for several years.
The sales price of komax amounts to 100 million Swiss francs and Koch retains a 44 percent stake.
More than 40 percent of the purchase price is financed through equity and part of the price also depends on the future success of komax.
SBC Equity Partners is the largest stake holder with 46 percent, while komax management's has a 10 percent stake. SBC's stake is held through its controlled unit, Indelec Holding AG.
The overall financing volume amounts to around 120 million francs, including operating credit requirements.
In 1995 komax, which employs 350 people, reported sales of 117 million francs and cash flow of 14.8 million.

Komax, founded in 1975, said it has a world market share of 40 percent in wire processing machinery and a sales and service network in more than 45 countries. It has assembly plants in Dierikon, Chicago and Parede, Portugal
